text.content:
The eldest @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} of the Carpathian line still spoken of by name, Yorak assumed the mantle of Voivode when the clan's Antediluvian — the Eldest — fell into torpor following an attack by the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri} knight Samiel. Reputedly the first koldun, Yorak withdrew into the caves where the demon-spirit Kupala whispered loudest, spending centuries enslaving tribes of Slavs, Celts, and Thracians for his experiments and pursuing Azhi Dahaka, the ecstatic transcendence at the heart of the Path of Metamorphosis. His magnum opus, the Cathedral of Flesh, was a subterranean palace of living architecture — pillars of grafted bodies, walls of singing mouths, windows of stretched and preserved skin — built over centuries with thousands of victims, and became the center of Metamorphosist thought and worship. No one now knows where it stood; where it once rose, only a gaping hole remains.

Uninterested in kingship, Yorak instead Embraced influential tribal leaders and let them handle politics on his behalf, most famously the shaman-goddess Shaagra. He reputedly fell during the chaos of the Anarch Revolt, though the culprit remains a mystery even to his own clan.

A Slavic shaman of the Vroi tribe who ruled her people as goddess, leader, and mystic before Yorak Embraced her, passing over rivals Triglav the Three-Headed and Lambach Ruthven in the process (a slight Lambach never forgot). Shaagra's Embrace precipitated the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} practice of claiming stock from noble families and tribal leaders to influence the region's mortals, giving rise to the revenant families. She never knew her sire, and once trained in @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} ways and bound by blood oath, she and her tribe followed her granddaughter and favored ghoul, Libuse, into the Danube Plain, eventually settling land that would become Prague — the westernmost point of Carpathian @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} influence and, later, a flashpoint of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}-Tzimisce conflict. Shaagra herself slept in fitful torpor in Kupala-tainted soil, growing steadily more insane with the passing centuries.

A Methuselah of ancient Carpathian nobility, passed over for Shaagra's Embrace in favor of Triglav the Three-Headed and never forgetting the insult. Despite that old grudge, Lambach attended Kupala's Eve when the young @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} broke their sires' blood oaths, and unlike many elders never turned against the anarchs who did it — without his vitae, many Fiends doubt they could have broken their bonds at all. Other @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} dismiss him as a fool and a screw-up, but those who have dealt with him longer suspect he plays that role deliberately, the better to observe unnoticed.

Lambach has reputedly witnessed the Eldest itself twice in recent history: once when the diablerist Lugoj Blood-breaker attempted to drain it, and once beneath the streets of New York. Some among the clan whisper that this is no coincidence — that Lambach is, unknowingly, the Eldest's chronicler, kept alive by fragments of its strength precisely so that he might document the clan's actions while his sire's sire slumbers, and that he will survive until the Eldest's final awakening.

Descended from Noriz, the so-called Corrupter of Legions, Lugoj became the first voice of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} dissent against the clan's elders, vowing alongside his siblings never to be anyone's pawn again. Together with his ally Velya the Flayer, Lugoj spent decades searching the Carpathians for Kupala's sacred fire-flower, an artifact the young @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} hoped would shatter the blood bonds their sires held over them. When the pair found it, they gathered their fellow rebels on Kupala's Eve, broke the ancient bonds, and set the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} Anarch Revolt into motion.

Some accounts claim Lugoj later committed the Amaranth upon the torpid Eldest itself, only for the Antediluvian to turn the act back on him — meaning that Lugoj, now himself in torpor somewhere in the Carpathians, may in some sense be the Eldest reborn. Other, more skeptical elders insist Lugoj was merely the Eldest's chosen instrument all along, guided to the fire-flower (in truth a fragment of the Antediluvian's own flesh) so that it could sunder its progeny's old alliances and remake the clan's loyalties around itself once more.

Claimed by his followers to be the first childe of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} Antediluvian itself, the Dracon was a principal founder of Constantinople and, unlike his Carpathian kin, spoke out publicly against Kupala and the koldunic sorcery bound up with it. His disputes with the Balkan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} turned to open war after his grandchilde Gesu suffered a mysterious torpor the Dracon blamed on his Carpathian cousins; in retaliation, he ambushed the koldun Triglav the Three-Headed and deprived him of his namesake heads, while the Balkan @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} destroyed Byzantine Akoimetai monasteries in reply. That rift, which brought the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.ldyqw2o2gR45LxDO]{Obertus} revenant family into the clan's service as reparation, has never fully healed, even in the modern nights.

The Dracon's spiritual heirs, the Children of the Dracon, style themselves a knightly order atoning for some unnamed sin the clan committed — possibly Kupala's Night itself — and reject koldunic sorcery even as they remain within the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}, opposing nearly every policy the clan Voivode enacts. The Dracon himself has not been seen in the Final Nights; some Tzimisce believe he simply grew tired of Constantinople's fall and vanished into the wider Jyhad.

Not a Cainite at all, but a demon-spirit of the land itself, bound by ancient Lupine shamans deep within the Carpathians — the mountains were said to have been raised by their claws specifically to imprison it. When the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} Antediluvian learned to speak to Kupala through dreams, the two struck a bargain: the Eldest would free Kupala from its prison in exchange for magic and allegiance against their shared Lupine enemies. The pact succeeded, but Kupala remained bound to the soil of the Carpathians even after its release, unable to return to whatever hell or spirit-realm once claimed it. It took the mountains as its new domain instead, sharing its existence — and its madness — with the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} ever since.

Kupala is the source of the clan's practice of koldunic sorcery, its curse of ancestral soil dependence, and (some koldun believe) the reason the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} sleep uneasily even in their own homeland: their rituals do not ward off Kupala's influence so much as earn the demon's favor for being obedient. Kupala is widely blamed for corrupting the soil of Eastern Europe and for the strange fertility of Tzimisce sorcery in the modern nights, when so many neonates who should have no access to the old ways have somehow rediscovered them.

The hoary eldest of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.lo3JcX4zfCMF8bOW]{Zantosa} household in New York, encountered by Lambach Ruthven at one of the family's decadent fetes. Where most @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.lo3JcX4zfCMF8bOW]{Zantosa} hide their venom under charm, Istvan wears his age openly, leering and whispering in a voice Lambach compared to a scream reverberating through subterranean caverns, and pressing on younger Fiends the family's chilling watchword: “Be a good lad.” Istvan's brownstone conceals catacombs that connect to the New York subways and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu}'s own sewer warrens — tunnels so extensive that not even the eldest Sewer Rats claim to know them in their entirety, leaving ample dark places for things — or someone — to hide. His tapping cane, thrice against the brownstone floor, seems a signal understood by more than one attentive listener beneath the city.

The name New York @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} give to the night, roughly 550 years past, when Lugoj Blood-breaker stood alone and rampant within a crumbling church and tore aside its flagstones to reveal something Lambach Ruthven cannot bring himself to describe even in a private diary written for a lover seven centuries dead. The clan's rebellious childer still reenact it every Christmas Eve as a solstice Rite, stalking Greenwich Village, Harlem, and the Upper West Side, gorging on the terror-laced vitae of manufactured “suicides,” “domestic disputes,” and “missing persons,” and throwing their heads back to howl in the old tongues. To most Fiends it is a proud and holy memorial of the Anarch Revolt's founding violence; to Lambach, five and a half centuries have not dulled its horror, and he alone seems to grasp what — or who — was actually uncovered beneath that church floor.

By Lambach Ruthven's account, New York is the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce}'s true stronghold in the Final Nights — the soul of the sect, in his words — hosting close to ten million kine across its metropolitan area to sustain the clan's appetite. The city's Seraphs, the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce}'s ruling council beneath the sect, meet here, and the Voivode is said to periodically call the wider clan to gather among its skyscrapers, making the city home to one of the most concentrated registries of @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} luminaries anywhere in the world. Beneath the glittering towers lies another New York: catacombs beneath @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.lo3JcX4zfCMF8bOW]{Zantosa} brownstones connecting to subway tunnels and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.UhaIbwzsC1O2x9vr]{Nosferatu} sewer warrens beyond any single Kindred's full mapping, a hidden geography Lambach suspects hides secrets even the city's eldest have not fully reckoned with.

vtmlarp.source: Clanbook: Tzimisce, Chapter One: A Rabble of Fiends & Chapter Two: Ego and Evolution; Libellus Sanguinis I: Masters of the State, Book Two: Tzimisce (Appendix: From the Diary of Lambach Ruthven)
